findings.body: javac fails with "method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types", so the whole build breaks and no runtime behavior of the fix is reachable.
findings.failure_mode: Compilation failure of the services module.
findings.impact: javac fails with "method isConditionalPasskeysEnabled in class UsernamePasswordForm cannot be applied to given types", so the whole build breaks and no runtime behavior of the fix is reachable.
findings.root_cause: The helper was introduced with a `UserModel` parameter in UsernamePasswordForm while the new call site in UsernameForm was written against a parameterless signature.
findings.suggested_fix: Either call `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` here, or add the intended no-argument helper (e.g. `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() { return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled(); }`) to UsernamePasswordForm and keep both call shapes consistent.
findings.title: UsernameForm calls isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() with no arguments, but only a UserModel overload exists
findings.trigger: Compiling the services module after this patch; the only definition introduced is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in UsernamePasswordForm and no no-argument overload exists anywhere in the tree (repository-wide search returns only the four sites in UsernameForm/UsernamePasswordForm).
findings.verifier_reason: The patch at UsernameForm.java:47 calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition introduced in UsernamePasswordForm.java:160 is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` which requires a UserModel parameter. The literal search confirms only the parameterized version exists. This is a compilation error.

raw_findings.body: `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked for the anonymous login page, so the conditional-UI attributes (challenge, rpId, enableWebAuthnConditionalUI) are not set and the `<form id="webauth">` / passkey autofill is no longer rendered — ID-less passkey login regresses, contradicting the unchanged assertions such as `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), Matchers.notNullValue());` right after `oauth.openLoginForm()`.
raw_findings.evidence: return webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null;
raw_findings.failure_mode: Passkey/conditional-UI markup is silently omitted on the primary login screen, breaking passwordless login and existing integration assertions.
raw_findings.impact: `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is never invoked for the anonymous login page, so the conditional-UI attributes (challenge, rpId, enableWebAuthnConditionalUI) are not set and the `<form id="webauth">` / passkey autofill is no longer rendered — ID-less passkey login regresses, contradicting the unchanged assertions such as `MatcherAssert.assertThat(driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")), Matchers.notNullValue());` right after `oauth.openLoginForm()`.
raw_findings.root_cause: The refactored guard replaced the previous `context.getUser() == null` condition with an inverted `user != null` requirement instead of making the check user-independent.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Drop the `user != null` term (the check should only be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`), so passkeys are set up both for the anonymous login page and for re-authentication.
raw_findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, disabling conditional passkeys on the ID-less login form
raw_findings.trigger: A realm with PASSKEYS enabled and WebAuthnPolicyPasswordless passkeys enabled; a fresh (non re-authentication) request opens the username/password login page, so `context.getUser()` is null in `authenticate()` (line 115) and in `challenge(context, error, field)` (line 137).

raw_findings.root_cause: The new override was added without the `@Override` annotation used by the other overriding methods in the class.
raw_findings.title: New override shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators is missing @Override
raw_findings.trigger: Any future change of the parent signature in WebAuthnAuthenticator (e.g. adding a parameter) while this method keeps the old signature.

raw_findings.body: The catch block swallows the unrelated failure and the assertion "no webauthn button" passes spuriously, so a real regression that renders the passkey form during password-only re-authentication would not be detected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Test can pass while the asserted condition is violated, weakening review/CI signal.
raw_findings.impact: The catch block swallows the unrelated failure and the assertion "no webauthn button" passes spuriously, so a real regression that renders the passkey form during password-only re-authentication would not be detected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new negative assertion was implemented with a generic exception-swallowing try/catch instead of a typed assertThrows.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the try/fail/catch blocks with `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, () -> driver.findElement(By.xpath("//form[@id='webauth']")));`, matching the pattern already used elsewhere in the passkeys tests.
raw_findings.title: Broad catch(Exception) instead of assertThrows hides unexpected WebDriver failures
raw_findings.trigger: `driver.findElement(...)` throws something other than NoSuchElementException (e.g. StaleElementReferenceException, WebDriverException on a broken page render) while the webauth form is actually present.

raw_findings.body: A regression where a re-authenticating user who has no WebAuthn passwordless credential is presented with a non-functional passkey prompt (or fails the flow) would go undetected by CI.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Untested branch of the changed authenticator logic; review cannot confirm the passkey-less re-authentication path.
raw_findings.impact: A regression where a re-authenticating user who has no WebAuthn passwordless credential is presented with a non-functional passkey prompt (or fails the flow) would go undetected by CI.
raw_findings.root_cause: The behavior change introduced by the unconditional `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators() == false` override is only tested with passkeys disabled at realm level.

raw_findings.title: No coverage for re-authentication of a passkey-less user in a passkeys-enabled realm
raw_findings.trigger: The new `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` returning false removes the `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() -> return null` guard for identified users, so during re-authentication the passkey UI is now filled even for a user with no passkeys registered; this test only exercises the case where the realm-level `WebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled` is FALSE, which short-circuits before that code path.

validated_findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that keeps `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.TRUE)` but uses a user without any passwordless WebAuthn credential, and assert the expected re-authentication behavior (password-only form works and no broken passkey prompt).
validated_findings.title: No coverage for re-authentication of a passkey-less user in a passkeys-enabled realm
validated_findings.trigger: The new `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` returning false removes the `authenticators.getAuthenticators().isEmpty() -> return null` guard for identified users, so during re-authentication the passkey UI is now filled even for a user with no passkeys registered; this test only exercises the case where the realm-level `WebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled` is FALSE, which short-circuits before that code path.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: This is a test coverage suggestion, not a bug in the patch. The candidate acknowledges the test uses `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)` and suggests additional coverage for passkeys-enabled realm with passkey-less user. This is a test gap observation, not a defect introduced by the patch. The existing test validates the stated scenario.
